results.title: B200 Spot −31%; Long-Term +94%? | BENQUAN Global
highlights:
## Quick Take

Quick Take: GPU rental entered a rare split in June 2026. B200 spot fell 31% in three weeks ($6.11 to $4.22/hr) as NVIDIA Blackwell capacity arrived. But long-term B200 contracts jump 94% ($2.63 to $5.10/hr) in October — same GPU, opposite price moves. B300 spot holds at $9.87/hr with 12-15 month lead times.

...

Channel rental split cited on this page (June–October 2026 window): B200 spot fell about 31% in three weeks ($6.11 to $4.22/hr) as Blackwell capacity arrived, while long-term B200 contracts jumped about 94% ($2.63 to $5.10/hr) in October—same GPU, opposite curves. Use the split to decide spot vs reservation length; confirm live $/hr before you model TCO.

...

Quick Answer: B200 spot pricing fell from $6.11 per hour to $4.22 per hour between late May and mid-June 2026, while B200 long-term contracts rose from $2.63 per hour toward a projected $5.10 per hour for October renewals. The same graphics processing unit moved in opposite directions within one month.

## Why Long-Term Is Surging: The Agent Inference Reckoning

Quick Answer: AI Agent workloads are driving inference demand that exceeds training demand growth. Cloud providers see 3-5 year forward demand curves they cannot satisfy with current capacity, so they are raising long-term prices to ration forward allocation and fund new data center builds.

- B200 renewal +94%: Baseten disclosed in May 2026 that its upstream cloud provider notified a B200 GPU lease renewal increase from $2.63/hr to $5.10/hr, effective October 2026 — a 94% jump. This is not negotiation; it is a unilateral supplier notice in a seller's market.
- B300 12-15 month lead time: A 1000-GPU B300 order placed today ships in Q3-Q4 2027. The allocation queue is already oversubscribed through 2027.
- Nebius +30% across the board: Nebius raised H100, H200, and B200 prices by roughly 30% effective June 1, 2026 — covering both on-demand and reserved contracts.
- NVIDIA FY27Q1 earnings call: Management explicitly stated "Agentic AI era has arrived" and confirmed H100 lease prices have risen ~20% year-to-date (with a cumulative ~38% from the October 2025 trough).
- Not temporary: Unlike the spot dip, the long-term price increase is structural. Cloud providers are pricing for a world where GPU demand doubles every 12-18 months and supply grows at 20-30% annually.

...

At $5.10/hr for B200 long-term, a 24/7 annual cost is approximately $44,676 per GPU. The equivalent B200 hardware purchase (at $45,000-$50,000 street) plus facility, cooling, and networking costs roughly the same over 24-36 months. Cloud providers are pricing long-term contracts to match or exceed the total cost of ownership for self-owned hardware — and they are getting it because the 12-15 month delivery wait for new hardware makes the "buy" option functionally unavailable for most buyers.

...

Quick Answer: Every major graphics processing unit cloud platform is running the same playbook: cut spot prices to attract developer mindshare and experimentation, then raise long-term prices to monetize committed enterprise workloads. This is not a contradiction but a deliberate two-tier strategy, so procurement plans should budget for both tiers separately.

| Platform | Spot Move | Long-Term Move | Strategy Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseten | Competitive spot | B200 +94% in Oct | Aggressive long-term repricing; NVIDIA-backed |
| Nebius | Matching market | +30% across H100/H200/B200 | Balanced two-tier; pan-generation increase |
| CoreWeave | H200 $6.31/hr spot | Long-term by quote | Premium positioning; B200 $8.60/hr spot |
| Lambda/Vast.ai | Aggressive spot ($0.74 H200) | Reserved 15-30% below on-demand | Volume play; spot as loss leader |
| AWS/Azure/GCP | Stable premium | Enterprise agreements | Not competing on spot; indirect beneficiaries |

...

GPU cloud providers have a fixed cost base (hardware depreciation) and variable revenue. A 20% increase in long-term pricing flows almost entirely to profit margin — operating leverage is extreme. Short-term spot discounts are marketing spend: they acquire developers who later convert to committed workloads. The two-tier strategy maximizes both adoption and monetization.

...

Quick Answer: The widest divergence sits in B200, where spot pricing fell thirty-one percent while long-term contracts rose ninety-four percent. B300 shows no spot relief at $9.87 per hour, H100 is being displaced toward lower tiers, and H200 holds steady as the mid-range option for buyers balancing memory capacity against hourly rate.

results.title: GPU cloud economico para entrenar IA: AITECH desde $2,4
highlights:
En pocas palabras: AITECH Cloud, el marketplace de GPU on-demand de Solidus AI Tech, sumó nuevas regiones en Estados Unidos para cargas de trabajo de IA. Ofrece placas H100 desde USD 2,4 por hora, H200 desde USD 2,84 y L40s desde USD 0,8, hasta 80% más barato que los hiperscalers según la propia empresa (julio 2026).

AITECH Cloud es el marketplace de GPU on-demand de Solidus AI Tech que arrancó ofreciendo placas H100 desde USD 2,4 por hora, hasta un 80% más barato que los hiperscalers según la propia empresa (julio 2026). Es una opción de GPU cloud económico para entrenar IA sin suscripción ni lock-in, con créditos en cripto o fiat y despliegue en segundos.

AITECH Cloud (también llamada Compute Layer o AITECH Cloud Network) es la infraestructura de cómputo GPU de Solidus AI Tech para entrenamiento e inferencia de modelos de IA. Es un marketplace on-demand: pagás por hora de uso real, cargás créditos en cripto o fiat y lanzás la instancia en segundos, sin contratos ni permanencia mínima. Sus precios de lanzamiento van de USD 0,8 a USD 2,84 por hora por placa.

...

- Precios de lanzamiento: H100 desde USD 2,4/hr, H200 desde USD 2,84/hr y L40s desde USD 0,8/hr por placa, según el marketplace oficial de AITECH.
- Ahorro declarado: hasta 80% frente a proveedores tradicionales (julio 2026), sin suscripción ni bloqueo.
- Modelo: marketplace on-demand, con despliegue en 3 pasos (registro, créditos, launch) y bare metal a pedido.
- Regiones nuevas en USA: el título circula, pero AITECH solo habla de “global locations” sin listar regiones puntuales. Tomalo con pinzas.
- Para quién: startups y equipos de research que quieren probar antes de comprometerse con un hiperscaler.

...

## Precios de GPU en AITECH Cloud: H100, H200 y L40s en 2026

AITECH Cloud publica tres niveles de precio de lanzamiento: la H100 desde USD 2,4/hr para training de alto throughput, la H200 desde USD 2,84/hr para cargas intensivas en memoria, y la L40s desde USD 0,8/hr para inferencia y despliegue escalable. Son valores por placa. Ojo con un detalle importante.

El propio sitio aclara que estos precios son “exclusively for the initial release and are subject to change at a later date”. Traducido: son precios de lanzamiento (julio 2026) y pueden cambiar. Si estás armando un presupuesto a 6 meses, no los tomes como fijos. Habría que ver cómo se sostienen cuando la demanda apriete.

...

La foto rápida, con la H100 como referencia. Los precios de los hiperscalers salen de comparativas públicas de hasta julio 2026, no de AITECH.

| Proveedor | Precio H100 (aprox.) | Lock-in | Modelo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AITECH Cloud | USD 2,4/hr | No | Marketplace on-demand |
| GMI Cloud | ~USD 2,0/hr | No | GPU cloud |
| AWS | ~USD 6,88/hr | Alto | Hiperscaler |
| Azure | ~USD 12,29/hr | Alto | Hiperscaler |
| RunPod / Vast.ai | Variable (subasta) | No | Marketplace |

Eso sí: el precio por hora no lo es todo. Los hiperscalers ganan en uptime garantizado, soporte enterprise y catálogo de servicios integrados. Si tu carga es misión crítica y no podés bancar una caída, la “economía” del marketplace se puede volver cara. La matriz real incluye uptime, soporte y latencia de región, no solo el GPU-hour.

results.title: RunPod vs Vast.ai vs Paperspace 2026: qual GPU Cloud escolher?
highlights:
RunPod é a escolha mais equilibrada para ComfyUI, workers e endpoints de IA. Vast.ai reduz o preço bruto para quem aceita operar um marketplace e lidar com interrupções. Paperspace facilita notebooks e VMs guiadas, mas cobra mais pelas GPUs fortes. Compare o custo real antes de contratar.

...

### Preço por hora engana: calcule o Índice GPU-Hora Real

Preço por hora é apenas a primeira linha da conta. Uma GPU fica cara quando permanece ligada entre tarefas. Também fica cara quando exige muitas tentativas de configuração ou perde um trabalho sem checkpoint.

O Índice GPU-Hora Real é um critério prático. Some o valor de compute ao armazenamento persistente, ao tempo de setup, ao risco operacional e ao tempo de suporte. Não é uma métrica oficial dos provedores. É a forma como o Runzos interpreta os preços oficiais para uma decisão operacional.

A pesquisa usou US$ 1 = R$ 5,0851 em 24 de julho de 2026. Os valores abaixo são aproximações editoriais, sem IOF ou spread de cartão. RunPod e Vast.ai exibem preços dinâmicos. Confira o valor atual antes de criar uma máquina.

| GPU e plataforma | USD/h no snapshot | BRL/h aprox. | BRL por 4h aprox. | Leitura correta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RunPod RTX 4090 Secure | US$ 0,69 | R$ 3,51 | R$ 14,03 | Referência de Pod Secure. |
| Vast.ai RTX 4090 floor | US$ 0,33 | R$ 1,68 | R$ 6,71 | Piso de marketplace, sujeito a host e disponibilidade. |
| Paperspace A5000 | US$ 1,38 | R$ 7,02 | R$ 28,07 | Preço oficial de Machine. |
| RunPod A100 80GB Secure | US$ 1,39 | R$ 7,07 | R$ 28,27 | Referência de Pod Secure. |
| Vast.ai A100 PCIe floor | US$ 0,56 | R$ 2,85 | R$ 11,39 | Piso dinâmico de marketplace. |
| Paperspace A100-80G | US$ 3,18 | R$ 16,17 | R$ 64,68 | Preço oficial de Machine. |
| RunPod H100 PCIe Secure | US$ 2,89 | R$ 14,70 | R$ 58,78 | Referência de Pod Secure. |
| Vast.ai H100 PCIe floor | US$ 1,72 | R$ 8,75 | R$ 34,99 | Piso dinâmico de marketplace. |
| Paperspace H100 | US$ 5,95 | R$ 30,26 | R$ 121,03 | Capacidade e aprovação podem ser exigidas. |

Os valores do RunPod são um snapshot da página oficial de preços. Os valores da Vast.ai vêm das páginas de preço por GPU e das taxas ao vivo do marketplace. A documentação de preços da Paperspace lista A5000 a US$ 1,38/h, A6000 a US$ 1,89/h, A100-80G a US$ 3,18/h e H100 a US$ 5,95/h.

Uma sessão de quatro horas ajuda a comparar testes. Para uso contínuo, o resultado muda. Uma RTX 4090 RunPod no snapshot chegaria perto de R$ 2.561 mensais em 24/7. A Vast.ai ficaria perto de R$ 1.225. Esses números assumem 720 horas e ignoram descontos por reserva, interrupções, armazenamento e indisponibilidade.

Esse cenário mostra por que uma VM ligada o mês inteiro merece outro modelo de contratação.

...

O leitor deve interpretar “a partir de” com cautela. A página do produto anuncia H100 a partir de US$ 0,90 por hora. As páginas de preço por GPU mostraram, no snapshot da pesquisa, RTX 4090 a US$ 0,33/h, A100 PCIe a US$ 0,56/h e H100 PCIe a US$ 1,72/h. São referências de marketplace, não uma tarifa garantida.

As instâncias interruptible podem ficar 50% ou mais abaixo do on-demand, conforme a documentação de preços da Vast.ai. Em troca, elas podem ser pausadas. Reserved tende a dar desconto com maior estabilidade. Nunca compare uma instância interruptible com uma GPU Secure ou on-demand como se o risco fosse igual.

...

No snapshot da pesquisa, RunPod H100 PCIe Secure custa US$ 2,89/h, Vast.ai H100 PCIe parte de US$ 1,72/h e Paperspace H100 custa US$ 5,95/h. Os dois primeiros valores podem variar. Todos exigem consulta antes da compra.

results.title: Daily Investment Brief — July 30, 2026 | Signwl
highlights:
The dominant narrative this cycle is constraint-driven pricing bifurcation: markets with deep supply and multiple competing providers are remarkably stable — H100 on-demand in Virginia, London, and Madrid has moved less than 1% in 30 days — while thin-market, single-provider, and geography-constrained nodes are experiencing violent repricing. The Tel Aviv A100 80GB has surged +550% in a single month from $0.156/hr to $1.02/hr with zero competitive response; Texas H100 on-demand is up +20.4% in 30 days to $10.44/hr against a flat Virginia; South Africa has the highest on-demand H100 price in the entire dataset at $13.53/hr. These are not demand spikes — they are the fingerprint of grid-constrained, single-provider markets where price is being set by whoever showed up first. Simultaneously, Google's TPU v7 is debuting across two regions at a deliberate premium above H100 equivalents ($10.28/hr London vs. $8.20/hr H100 London), and AWS has successfully contracted $225B of forward Trainium demand. The market structure story — who controls power, who controls supply depth — is now more important than the headline GPU pricing level.

results.title: Implied Committed Rates: What the Big Compute Deals Pay per GPU-Hour · CCIR Research
highlights:
The headline mega-deals are negotiated committed-term prints, disclosed as lump sums rather than rates. This note backs the unit rate out of the disclosed figures, and every number it produces is a floor by construction.

...

> Spend is ratable across the full disclosed term. 100% of contracted hours are billed. All disclosed dollars are treated as compute, with no carve-out for power, networking, or services. Fleet size is constant over the term. 8,760 hours per year; 730 hours per month. Every one of these assumptions biases the implied rate downward. All figures are therefore floors on blended committed rates, not observed prices.

...

## 03 The GPU-hour table

| Deal | Chip | Disclosed | Implied rate | Grade |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft–Nscale/Aker (Narvik) | GB300 disclosed | $6.2B · 5 yr · ~52,000 GPUs | $2.72/GPU-hr | A |
| Anthropic–xAI (SpaceX) | unspecified NVIDIA, no model filed | $1.25B/month through May 2029 · ~325,000 GPUs | $5.27/GPU-hr | A |
| Microsoft–IREN | GB300 disclosed | $9.7B · 5 yr · 200MW critical IT load | ~$2.2/GPU-hr CCIR estimate | A MW basis |
| Microsoft–Nebius | GB300 per press | $17.4B (up to $19.4B with added GPUs) · 5 yr · ">100,000" GPUs (press) | $3.97/GPU-hr | B |
| OpenAI–AWS | GB200/GB300 disclosed | $38B · 7 yr · "hundreds of thousands" of GPUs + CPUs | $1.24–$3.10/GPU-hr (band) | B |

All rows: implied — computed by CCIR from the disclosed figures; floors per §02.

...

Anthropic–xAI is the fee-basis print. SpaceX's prospectus discloses the terms verbatim: "the customer has agreed to pay us $1.25 billion per month through May 2029," for compute capacity that "includes approximately 325,000 NVIDIA GPUs" across the COLOSSUS facilities. A monthly fee needs no term assumption: $1.25B ÷ (325,000 × 730 hours) = $5.27. Three caveats travel with the row. Either party may terminate on 90 days' notice after an initial three-month period, so the contract prices like a short-tenor rate wearing a 2029 end date. The filing names no GPU generation, so the row is not part of the GB300 set below and no spread against it is computed. And capacity ramped through May and June 2026 at a reduced fee.
